​Build open agents that work together

​The Collaborative Agent Hackathon is a one-day event for building open-source, collaborative AI agents with Flower.

​Agents are changing what’s possible. We’ll explore how they can achieve more by working together safely in human-supervised multi-agent teams.

​You’ll form a team on the day, build a working prototype, and demo it at the end of the event. Projects can range from simple agent collaborations to more complex systems that delegate tasks, share context, and coordinate their work.

​You don’t need an existing team or a fully developed idea. Bring your laptop, your interests, and a willingness to collaborate.

WHAT IS re:AGENT

re:AGENT is a two-day build weekend focused on the infrastructure scientific agents still need: better datasets, sharper tools, and reliable ways to evaluate their work. Participants will use Paperclip , Proto , Claude , and other scientific AI tools to build systems that can take on real scientific problems and produce results worth trusting.
Paperclip turns papers, datasets, clinical trials, and biological databases into an agent-native workspace that AI systems can search, synthesize, and build upon. Proto is a design framework and infrastructure layer for generative biology, allowing builders to combine AI models and search for DNA, RNA, or protein sequences that satisfy custom criteria.
The weekend brings together engineers, scientists, computational biologists, founders, and AI researchers. Projects might include assembling a research-ready dataset that would be impractical to create by hand, along with the analysis needed to show that its findings are real. Others might involve designing a new biological system to a defined specification and testing whether it holds up against existing evidence.
The aim is not just to accelerate existing workflows, but to create the tools, datasets, and evaluation methods that make entirely new scientific questions and experiments possible.

About Event
​Build It. Test It. Prove It.

​Looks like a hackathon. Runs like a pressure test on you, not just your idea.

​Proving Ground runs a free three-day Sprint where judges push past the pitch. No script survives real questions about what you tried, what broke, and what you changed.

​Past teams have gone on to raise from 500 Global and Blitzscaling Ventures and join Berkeley SkyDeck and Confluent's accelerator. Those decisions were made independently of Proving Ground.

​What this is

​Most events judge what you built by the end. We watch the process and look past the end to what comes next.

​The team is almost everything: how you make decisions under pressure, how you handle a setback, how you treat each other when something breaks. You'll document that as you go. What we ask you to show, and how we question it, is built around behavior, not performance.

​Two tracks

​Discovery Track. Pre-market, no active customer contact yet. For founders seriously exploring a startup, including enterprise folks weighing the leap.

​Pre-Seed Track. In-market, already talking to customers. Ship something real, show what's changed, pressure-test your next move.

​The prize: the Street Test

​There's no cash and no trophy. Teams that clear the Sprint's scoring bar earn the Street Test: 30 days back in the real world, with no artificial deadline and no audience. It's a bar, not a placement, so any team that clears it gets in. This is where we see whether momentum was real or borrowed from the room.

​Teams that complete it receive a Proving Ground report card: a scored record of how you operated across the Sprint and the Street Test, scored on Pull, Momentum, and Founder Fit. It's yours to share with investors.

​It's the part a hackathon can't offer, because a hackathon ends when the event does.

The legal industry touches nearly everyone and has changed less than almost any other sector in the last few decades — this weekend is about building the tools that could finally change that, from AI that helps a tenant fight an eviction to software that lets a small business draft a contract without a $400-an-hour phone call.

About Event

Jev is a new kind of model from TypeSafe AI. It takes unstructured context and returns typed, probabilistic decisions that software can act on.
Using Jev well changes how you design workflows. You have to decide which judgments belong to the model, how to frame those decisions, and when the result should trigger an action, human review, or escalation. The fastest way to develop that instinct, or understand the “Jevability” of a problem, is to build.
Join us at the PromptQL office on Tuesday, September 29, from 4–7 p.m. PT for a hands-on evening exploring what becomes possible when decisions get fast, structured, and cheap.
We’ll start with a lightning session dissecting the architecture of four or five real systems built with Jev, and show off some of the best builds from the previous session. We’ll look at patterns such as routing work, selecting from existing options, ranking evidence, verifying agent output, and turning confidence into reliable control flow.
Then we’ll hack.
Bring a workflow, product idea, or recurring judgment you want to rebuild. You’ll leave with a working prototype, a sharper sense of where Jev fits, and practical patterns you can reuse in future systems.
